messages.subject: Question on pooling data
parts:
To DISTANCE users:



I am unsure what is the best way to pool my data, I have line transect data
from annual game counts over several years, with repetitions, and through
diverse vegetation types. Any advice would be very helpful....



My data set:



7 years (with 8-16 repetitions per year) of data of observations of 14
ungulate species along 8 line-transects through various amounts of 11
vegetation types.



I wish to find the long-term average density of each species per vegetation
type.



Firstly, I have analysed the data by pooling all the transects for all the
years and repetitions and stratifying for vegetation types. This gives me a
nice number of observations, to work out the density estimate per vegetation
type, and gives me the overall average density across the years, (which is
what I am interested in). However, I now realize the sample size is 1, and
so my variance is inaccurate - right?



Can boot-strapping solve this problem?



Could I:



1.. Use the transects as samples and pool years and repetitions. However
not all transects pass through all the vegetation types, and some vegetation
types are crossed by a single transect.
2.. Pool all the transects and repetitions and use the years as samples,
stratifying for vegetation. However the number of observations will drop and
probably be too low in the smaller vegetation areas.
I would then need the average density per strata across the years /
transects, and if I took the mean density, would I lose the confidence
intervals anyway?



Thank you in advance, for any help. My email address is jj...@kent.ac.uk I
will be summarise any relevant replies and post them on the message board.



Julian Easton.
